ci_method: Callaway-Sant'Anna (2021) doubly-robust group-time ATTs aggregated with weights proportional to the number of treated county-years in each (cohort, year) cell (the 'simple' aggregation, which is exactly the ATT across treated county-years); 95% CI from the multiplier bootstrap clustered at the county level (5,000 draws), SE = 0.217. Corroborated by a nonparametric county-level bootstrap (400 reps, SE = 0.209, percentile CI [6.74, 7.63]), by CS analytic influence-function SEs (CI [6.77, 7.59]), and by Sun-Abraham/fixest with county-clustered SEs (7.179, CI [6.81, 7.55]).
specifications_run: Descriptive: cohort-by-year outcome means and first differences (cohorts 2006 n=146, 2011 n=71, 2016 n=57, never-treated n=26); verified panel is balanced (300 counties x 16 years), no missing outcomes, and that `program` == 1{year >= adoption_year} with zero mismatches

Static two-way FE OLS: new_biz_per_10k ~ program | county + year, county-clustered SE -> -0.447 (95% CI [-0.867, -0.027]). DISCARDED: this is the Goodman-Bacon/de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille bias - with staggered adoption and effects that grow with exposure, already-treated counties serve as controls, and the forbidden comparisons flip the sign

Two-way FE + county-specific linear time trends: +0.828 (95% CI [0.673, 0.983]). DISCARDED as the headline: county trends absorb most of the genuine dynamic (exposure-growing) treatment effect, so it is biased toward zero for this estimand
PRIMARY - Callaway-Sant'Anna, never-treated controls, doubly robust, 'simple' aggregation (treated-county-year weights): 7.179, SE 0.217, CI [6.754, 7.605]
Callaway-Sant'Anna, not-yet-treated controls, simple aggregation: 7.038, SE 0.149, CI [6.746, 7.329]
Callaway-Sant'Anna, never-treated controls, universal base period: 7.179 (unchanged)
Callaway-Sant'Anna with analytic influence-function SEs instead of bootstrap: 7.179, SE 0.209, CI [6.770, 7.589]
Sun-Abraham interaction-weighted event study (fixest::sunab, never-treated as reference), aggregated to overall ATT: 7.179, SE 0.188, CI [6.809, 7.550]
Callaway-Sant'Anna full group-time ATT(g,t) matrix, all 3 cohorts x all years, incl. pre-treatment placebo cells
Callaway-Sant'Anna dynamic (event-time) aggregation, e = -10 to +14
Callaway-Sant'Anna cohort aggregation: 2006 -> 8.296, 2011 -> 5.401, 2016 -> 3.028 (differences driven by exposure length, not cohort-specific effectiveness)
Callaway-Sant'Anna on a balanced event window e=0..4 only (all three cohorts contribute): 3.169, CI [2.831, 3.508] - the same underlying effect path, just a shorter-exposure estimand

Callaway-Sant'Anna dropping the 2006 cohort entirely (it has only one pre-period): 4.721, CI [4.314, 5.128]. Lower only because dropping the long-exposure cohort changes the exposure mix of the estimand, not because of bias
Differential linear pre-trend test, 2011 cohort vs never-treated, pre-2011 data only: 0.049 per year (95% CI [-0.072, 0.170])
Differential linear pre-trend test, 2016 cohort vs never-treated, pre-2016 data only: 0.027 per year (95% CI [-0.016, 0.070])
Pooled differential linear pre-trend (2011+2016 cohorts, own pre-periods): 0.027 per year (95% CI [-0.015, 0.069])
In-time placebo: 2016 cohort recoded as adopting in 2011, estimated on pre-2016 data only: -0.041 (CI [-0.564, 0.481])
In-time placebo: 2011 cohort recoded as adopting in 2008, estimated on pre-2011 data only: -0.044 (CI [-0.585, 0.498])

Rambachan-Roth-style linear-trend sensitivity: hand-coded bias correction subtracting delta*(e+1) from every post-treatment ATT(g,t) under the treated-county-year weights, swept over delta = 0 to 1.2 per year; breakdown value (ATT = 0) is delta ~ 1.03 per year
Nonparametric county-level cluster bootstrap of the primary estimate, 400 resamples of counties with replacement: SE 0.209, percentile CI [6.742, 7.625]
Cross-cohort consistency check: ATT(g,e) compared across the three cohorts at common event times e=0..4
assumptions_checked: Treatment definition / data integrity: confirmed `program` equals 1{year >= adoption_year} for all 4,800 rows, panel balanced at 300 counties x 16 years, no missing outcomes, 3,185 treated county-years. Verified the treated-county-year weights (2006: 2,190; 2011: 710; 2016: 285) and that my manual weighted aggregation of ATT(g,t) reproduces the package's 7.179 exactly
No-anticipation: CS pre-treatment placebo cells at e = -2, -3, -4, -5 are small and insignificant (-0.150, 0.172, 0.043, -0.001), so no run-up in the year(s) before adoption
Parallel trends (joint pre-test): CS Wald pre-test p = 0.69 with never-treated controls, p = 0.74 with not-yet-treated controls - no evidence against parallel trends in the testable pre-periods

Parallel trends (pre-trend slope): differential linear pre-trend is 0.027 per year pooled (95% CI [-0.015, 0.069]); 0.049 for the 2011 cohort and 0.027 for the 2016 cohort, both insignificant. The 2016 cohort gives 11 clean pre-periods

Parallel trends (in-time placebos): two fake adoption dates estimated purely on pre-treatment data both return essentially zero (-0.04), so the never-treated counties do track treated counties absent the program

Parallel trends (sensitivity / breakdown analysis): the exposure-weighted mean of (e+1) across treated county-years is 7.0, so a violation of delta per year biases the ATT by ~7*delta. Killing the result requires delta ~ 1.03 per year, about 15x the upper 95% bound on the measured pre-trend (0.069) and ~25 SEs away. The sign is robust by a very wide margin

Unverifiable extrapolation for the 2006 cohort: it has only one pre-period (2005), so its parallel trend cannot be tested directly, and it supplies 69% of treated county-years and all of the long-exposure cells (e=10..14). Checked indirectly, and it passes: at common event times e=0..4 its ATTs (1.35, 2.46, 3.40, 4.13, 5.42) nearly coincide with the 2011 cohort (0.51, 1.91, 3.43, 3.88, 4.83) and the 2016 cohort (0.92, 2.22, 3.03, 3.85, 5.12), both of which have clean pre-periods

Staggered-adoption / negative-weight problem in TWFE: diagnosed directly by contrasting static TWFE (-0.447) with heterogeneity-robust CS (+7.179) and Sun-Abraham (+7.179); the dynamic aggregation shows effects rising monotonically from 1.04 at e=0 to 15.61 at e=14, exactly the pattern that makes already-treated controls contaminate TWFE
Control-group choice: never-treated (7.179) vs not-yet-treated (7.038) give materially the same answer, so the result does not hinge on the small never-treated group (26 counties)

Comparability of the never-treated group in levels: 2005 means are 11.09 (never-treated) vs 10.32 / 10.02 / 10.48 for the three cohorts - no large level gap that would make the comparison strained (and CS requires parallel trends, not equal levels)

Inference robustness with few control clusters (26 never-treated counties): CS multiplier bootstrap (SE 0.217), CS analytic influence function (SE 0.209), Sun-Abraham county-clustered (SE 0.188), and an independent nonparametric county-level cluster bootstrap (SE 0.209, CI [6.74, 7.63]) all agree, so the interval is not an artifact of one SE formula

Estimand definition: confirmed that the requested 'average over all treated county-years' corresponds to CS 'simple' aggregation. Noted that because effects grow with exposure, this estimand is exposure-weighted and is not the effect of a typical year of program participation for a newly adopting county (that is ~1.0 in year 0, ~3.2 averaged over the first five years)
headline_claim: Counties in the small-business grant program averaged 7.2 more new business registrations per 10,000 residents (95% CI 6.8 to 7.6) than they would have without the program, averaged across all program county-years, with the effect building steadily from about 1 per 10,000 in the first year to about 16 per 10,000 after 14 years of participation.
